BIM Group partners with IRONMAN: From the Hawai'i model to the Phu Quoc aspiration.
sum: The story of the IRONMAN race's development in Hawai'i is a classic example of how sporting events can be linked to tourism and leisure, enhancing the appeal of a coastal and island destination. In partnership with this global sporting event brand, BIM Group strives to make Phu Quoc one of the world's leading tourist destinations, where the journey of conquest is extended by experiences beyond the race track.

The Hawai'i Islands are the birthplace of IRONMAN, with the first race held on Oʻahu in 1978. In 1981, for traffic safety reasons, the race moved to Kailua-Kona, on the west side of the Big Island. Here, the lava fields lining the route became the iconic backdrop for the endurance challenge, becoming an integral part of the race's image for decades.

For athletes, Kona - Hawai'i is associated with the aspiration to conquer the highest peaks. Through images of the competition, the landscapes of Hawai'i also reach the global sports community. This connection shows how an international event can add depth to the destination experience: the competition journey opens up opportunities to explore nature, relax, and spend time with loved ones.

This is also the direction that BIM Group is pursuing in Phu Quoc, partnering with Sunrise Events Vietnam to bring IRONMAN series races to the island since 2022. Built on the foundation of the resort development at Phu Quoc Marina, sporting events create another reason for tourists to choose Phu Quoc and experience the island.

When Mark Allen, a six-time IRONMAN World Championship winner, visited Phu Quoc as an inspirational ambassador in 2024, he recognized the similarities between the island and Kona. He encouraged athletes to share their experiences with the race and the organization in Phu Quoc with their communities.

While the Kona race track evokes the atmosphere of lava fields, Phu Quoc offers a racing experience set against a tropical backdrop, with long stretches of sand and turquoise waters at Bai Truong Beach. The landscape contributes to the race's unique character, while also providing opportunities for relaxation and recreation for athletes and their families.
Kailua-Kona and Bai Truong also share similarities in location, both situated on the western side of the island and close to the airport.

items.t: GSBIM turns laser scans into photorealistic building models with centimetre-level textures
sum: Building Information Models have become the standard digital backbone of construction and facility management, yet most as-built BIM reconstructions still look disappointingly plain. According to a new study published in Multimedia Tools and Applications, models rebuilt from real-world scans typically appear as bare geometric surfaces or rely on artificially assigned textures, an absence of real-world appearance that limits visual interpretability, reduces immersion in digital environments and restricts downstream tasks that depend on surface texture, such as defect detection and facility inspection. The paper, authored by Yuyang Jin, Siyi Li, Lihui Huang, Nanying Liang and Yiyu Cai, introduces a framework called GSBIM that fuses laser-scanned point clouds, industry-standard BIM geometry and a rapidly maturing 3D rendering technique known as Gaussian Splatting into a single photorealistic, metrically consistent model.

The core problem the researchers identify is one of disconnected pipelines. Existing image-to-BIM texture mapping methods often depend on image feature registration or manual alignment and can be affected by occlusions, the authors write. Meanwhile, Gaussian Splatting provides photorealistic view synthesis, but standard image-driven pipelines usually rely on Structure-from-Motion and produce standalone Gaussian representations that are not inherently constrained to the shared LiDAR and BIM metric frame. In other words, the visually striking renders produced by Gaussian Splatting have historically lived in their own coordinate universe, detached from the precisely measured BIM geometry that engineers and facility managers actually use. GSBIM addresses this by integrating IFC-based as-built BIM, point-cloud-derived IFC texture maps and geometry-constrained LiDAR Gaussian Splatting in a shared coordinate system, so that rendered output is anchored to the same metric frame as the underlying building model.

A key innovation lies in how the framework acquires its training views. Perspective training views and camera poses are derived from registered scanner panoramas and scan poses, avoiding manual alignment between images, point clouds and BIM geometry.

Why BIM Still Doesn't Know What Your Building Is Made Of
sum: Move a wall in Revit and every plan, section and schedule follows. Change a material, though, and the team is often back in specifications, spreadsheets and drawings, checking that they all describe the same choice.

For Dave Lemont, who led Revit Technology before Autodesk acquired it, that gap is BIM's unfinished work. Now Executive Chairman of Acelab, he is focused on a Material Intelligence Model: one structured product record, connected to every document where that selection appears. It is also something architects can now try for themselves, since Acelab has opened Material Hub search to anyone, no account required.
In this conversation, he discusses what connected material data means for architects and owners, where AI helps, and why the final call still belongs to the designer.
Eduardo Souza (ArchDaily): When you were bringing Revit to market, what did you hope to change about architectural practice?
Dave Lemont (Acelab): Everything was 2D. The plan, section, elevation and schedule were drawn separately, as unrelated drawings that happened to describe the same building. Move a

wall and someone had to find it again in each one and change it by hand. The breakthrough was the parametric building model: one model, with every drawing as a view of it. Change the model and the drawings update; edit a drawing and the model updates. The name Revit came from "revise instantly." The larger idea, which later took the name BIM, was that a building could be represented as intelligent objects carrying all the material information, not just geometry.
AD: Why is material information still so difficult to connect across tools and documents?

Why construction firms can’t afford outdated IT systems
sum: Construction may happen on site, but much of the work that keeps a project moving now happens digitally. Your team checks drawings on tablets, shares documents through the cloud, prices jobs using specialist software and communicates with subcontractors across multiple locations. Technology is also instrumental in the planning phase, with tools like 3D modelling and GPS mapping. As that reliance grows, ageing IT is more than an inconvenience. It can influence everything from your ability to win new business to how your projects run.

Outdated technology costs you in small increments – of money, of errors, of time – that eventually add up. Customers, clients and staff will become frustrated by long loading times, manual data entry and analysis, information errors, scattered files and outdated software and machinery that impact how effectively your company is able to perform.

Inefficient systems can also risk your ability to compete for new business. If you’re getting negative reviews relating to your speed, accuracy and responsiveness, customers are likely to go elsewhere. The most successful construction businesses aren’t simply reactive to the rapid progression of technology – they build IT into the core of the business plan.

Construction firms hold information that criminals can exploit, and it’s vital you build strong foundations against online threats to keep this data safe. Under the Data Protection Act 2018 and UK General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), you’re legally required to safeguard personal customer data. Your data, such as commercial documents, staff details, payment information and project plans, also requires protection from theft and fraud.

Older systems become particularly problematic when vendors stop supporting them, because your business may no longer receive the updates needed to address newly discovered vulnerabilities. The NCSC warns that construction businesses face threats including spear-phishing, ransomware and supply-chain attacks.

Identify unsupported operating systems and applications and apply available security updates or arrange replacements where necessary, according to risk. Even with new systems, strong cybersecurity relies on everyday controls.

items.t: Stefanutti Stocks : Re-Engineering Africa’s Built Environment
sum: Stefanutti Stocks is reshaping Southern Africa’s construction landscape through multidisciplinary expertise, digital innovation, and sustainable infrastructure solutions. Russell Crawford, CEO, tells us how the group continues to navigate challenges whilst building for future growth.

The construction industry in South Africa (SA) has evolved alongside the country’s built environment and urban growth, demonstrating resilience through successive periods of economic, social, and technological change.
Since the 19th century, the construction industry has had a profound impact on SA’s socioeconomic makeup, driven by the changing needs of the nation’s infrastructure and rapid technological change.
Construction has been closely linked to SA’s mining sector for more than a century, supporting industrialisation, urbanisation, labour mobility, and infrastructure development since the late 1800s.

Indeed, the growing mining industry at the time generated greater demand for critical infrastructure such as railways and bridges, logistics and transport, industrial buildings, roads, and evolving urban settlements.

The expansion and diversification of the construction industry was therefore not an isolated event, as it evolved in the early 1900s from local building activity into an increasingly multidisciplinary landscape concerning labour movement, transport, materials, and urbanisation.

The discovery of gold on the Witwatersrand in 1886 led directly to the founding of Johannesburg, which within a decade had become the country’s largest town. Into the 20th century, deep-level mining and a growing manufacturing base drove sustained investment in transport, industrial, and urban infrastructure.

HDAC1/2 maintain alveolar macrophage homeostasis through Bim and LSD1
sum: A study led by Professor Li Wu at the Institute of Immunology, Tsinghua University, was published in Volume 2 of the journal Immunity & Inflammation on October 19, 2026. The article reports that HDAC1 and HDAC2 are key epigenetic regulators of alveolar macrophages (AMs), jointly promoting their differentiation and survival. Combined deletion of HDAC1 and HDAC2 leads to severe AM loss, alveolar proteinosis-like pathological changes, and significantly increased susceptibility to influenza virus infection in mice.

AMs are among the most important tissue-resident macrophages in the lung. They serve as the first line of immune defense against respiratory pathogens and are essential for maintaining the metabolism of pulmonary surfactant and lung homeostasis. Multiple cytokines and transcription factors have been identified as regulators of AM development and differentiation; however, the role of epigenetic regulation in maintaining AM homeostasis has remained to be further clarified.

HDAC1 and HDAC2 belong to class I histone deacetylases. They share high sequence similarity and exhibit functional redundancy in many cell types. In this study, the researchers found that combined deletion of Hdac1 and Hdac2 led to near-complete loss of AMs, whereas deletion of Hdac1 or Hdac2 alone had no obvious effect on AM numbers. Using different Cre-driven conditional gene knockout systems and competitive bone marrow chimeric experiments, the team confirmed that HDAC1 and HDAC2 exert important cell-intrinsic regulatory effects on AM maintenance.

The study further showed that HDAC1/2 deficiency produces pathological consequences beyond macrophage loss. AMs not only maintain the alveolar environment but also form an important component of respiratory innate immune defense. Mice with combined HDAC1/2 deficiency displayed obvious alveolar proteinosis-like features, including significantly elevated total protein levels in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and accumulation of surfactant proteins in lung tissue.

sum: Electromech Infraprojects files DRHP for IPO with fresh issue of up to ₹326 crore

Electromech Infraprojects Ltd on Monday (October 26) said it has filed its Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) for an initial public offering (IPO) comprising a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to ₹326 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 18,91,000 equity shares by existing shareholders.
The DRHP, dated September 23, 2026, marks a step towards the company's proposed listing in the capital markets. The equity shares will have a face value of ₹5 each.

Electromech Infraprojects provides mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) solutions across data centres, Global Capability Centres (GCCs), and commercial and industrial projects. Its capabilities cover technical design, engineering, procurement, project execution, testing and commissioning.

The company's execution model integrates procurement, engineering and quality control, supported by project-management systems such as Building Information Modelling (BIM). The technology enables integrated three-dimensional modelling of its MEP scope to identify and resolve design clashes before site work begins.

As of March 31, 2026, the company had an order book of ₹829.72 crore across 45 ongoing projects. Data centres accounted for ₹729.46 crore (87.92%), GCCs for ₹37.36 crore (4.50%) and commercial and industrial projects for ₹62.90 crore (7.58%). The DRHP also identifies a 48 MW data-centre project in Telangana, with an order book value of ₹501 crore, exclusive of GST, as one of its larger ongoing assignments.
The contribution of repeat customers to revenue from operations increased from 87% in fiscal 2024 to 89% in fiscal 2025 and 95% in fiscal 2026, according to the DRHP.

sum: SpyGlass Pharma Announces Positive 4-Year Data From First-in-Human Trial of Its Innovative BIM-IOL System
Four-year interim data cover 21 evaluable patients, with 18 remaining off all topical eye-pressure-lowering drops.

Rhea-AI Sentiment reads the wording of the document, how positive or negative its language is on a 1 to 5 scale. The balance of points shown with the takes weighs what the document actually discloses, so the two can disagree, for example when a trial that missed its main goal is described in upbeat language.
SpyGlass Pharma (SGP) announced four-year interim results from its first-in-human trial of the Bimatoprost Drug Pad-IOL System, or BIM-IOL System.

The trial involves patients with mild-to-moderate open angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension undergoing routine cataract surgery. Among 21 evaluable patients, mean intraocular pressure, the pressure inside the eye, fell 37% across all three dose groups, from 25.1 ± 2.5 mmHg at baseline after washout to 15.9 ± 2.8 mmHg. At four years, 86% (18 of 21) remained off all topical pressure-lowering drops, and 90% maintained best corrected distance visual acuity of at least 20/25. No product-related adverse events were reported.
The trial was designed to evaluate safety and efficacy over seven years; the company plans to follow patients through 2029.

Autodesk’s most ambitious AI play yet
sum: At Autodesk University Autodesk presented an AI ambition that goes beyond faster tools: a connected Assistant that decides how to solve tasks on your behalf. But as Greg Corke found on the Expo floor, there’s also a growing appetite for local AI, keeping data and costs firmly under control

Autodesk no longer just wants to sell you better software; it wants to do a lot of your work for you. At Autodesk University 2026, that ambition was presented as ‘Project Intelligence’, described by Autodesk CEO Andrew Anagnost during his keynote as a “connected brain at the centre that brings every data point, every decision, every discipline together – a brain that grows smarter as a project advances.”

Naturally, AI dominated the agenda. Almost every major announcement came wrapped in talk of agents, models and context. What set this AU apart from the previous two, however, was a shift from talk of time-saving features in individual CAD and BIM tools to a more ambitious AI proposition: an intelligent AI intended to turn a user’s stated intent into work they can review, refine, and use, without them having to navigate products, workflows, data and complex UIs. In other words, users state what they want, and Autodesk becomes the orchestrator calling on the relevant tools from its broad software ecosystem.
The headline announcement was that Autodesk Assistant is going solo. Anagnost explained that it will be available as a “standalone agent-first experience, one that reaches across products.”

Mike Haley, SVP research gave the rationale in the pre-event press briefing stating that it is “for work that doesn’t fit neatly inside a product like Revit or AutoCAD or Fusion.” The software is still in development and expected to launch next year.

Standalone Assistant is not a replacement for the Assistants already found inside Revit, AutoCAD, Fusion, Civil 3D, Forma Data Management, Autodesk Build and others. In fact, Amy Bunszel, executive VP, AEC solutions, confirmed that Autodesk will keep expanding the in-product versions.

sum: The Digital Twin Market was valued at USD 39.45 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 53.60 billion in 2026 before climbing to USD 1,085.20 billion by 2035, registering a CAGR of 38.70% during the 2026–2035 forecast window. This acceleration is anchored in two converging forces: widespread industrial IoT platform maturation and a wave of government mandates requiring a real-time digital twin for energy grid management across safety-critical infrastructure in the US, EU, and China. The US Department of Energy's 2024 allocation of USD 1.2 billion toward grid modernization programs specifically earmarked digital-replica capabilities for transmission monitoring .

Physics-informed, cloud-native simulation environments combining sensor data, AI inference and 3D visualization replace legacy siloed SCADA and CAD-based design procedures. Global spending on enterprise IoT-based digital twin for smart manufacturing surpassed USD 8 billion in 2024, led by automotive OEMs and semiconductor fabs seeking 12–18% yield gains through virtual process optimization [3]. Industrial digital twin for predictive maintenance already underlies more than 40% of new condition monitoring contracts signed by Tier-1 equipment vendors .

North America holds over 41.0% of the Digital Twin Market, driven by defense-sector digital-thread programs and hyperscaler cloud spending. Asia-Pacific is the fastest expanding area at an expected 28.10% CAGR, fueled by China’s “Digital China 2035” vision and India’s Smart Cities Mission. Europe has the second-highest share at around 26.5%, with Germany and France leading the way in adoption in the automotive and aerospace sectors. The Digital Twin Market will change the way enterprises develop, run and decommission physical assets of all sizes during the next decade.

items.t: Bim Pepple leads the way but Plymouth Argyle are spreading goals around
sum: Argyle have scored 14 goals in league and cup this season and they have come from nine different players
Tom Cleverley believes Plymouth Argyle are making it difficult for other teams to defend against them because they can score goals in a variety of different ways.
The Pilgrims have netted 14 times this season - with 10 goals in six League One games, plus four more in a couple of Carabao Cup matches.

Those goals have been shared among nine players, with Bim Pepple leading the way on three after he was on target with Argyle's third goal in their 3-0 league win against Barnsley at Home Park on Saturday.

Xavier Amaechi, Will Evans and Oli Irow, the loan signing from Tottenham Hotspur, have all scored twice, while there has been one goal apiece for Ronan Curtis, Alex Hartridge, Julio Pleguezuelo, Caleb Watts and Harvey White.

Cleverley said: "It's really good we are a team that has different avenues of scoring. Set plays is an avenue, direct football like you saw from the kick-off (against Barnsley) is an avenue, controlled possession in their half is an avenue.

"Then quality and combinations like you saw at Wycombe is a different avenue. We are a hard team to prepare against to defend and that's because we have a spread of personnel who can score the goals and a spread of avenues to get them."

sum: The initiative involved preparing and serving meals at social institutions in Tete and Zambézia, as well as distributing food hampers to elderly people in Cabo Delgado, benefiting approximately 860 people, including children, older persons and other individuals in situations of greater social vulnerability.

In Tete, the activity took place at the Rainha da Paz Reception Centre. In Zambézia, the initiative was carried out at the Sinacura Open Centre. In Cabo Delgado, food hampers were distributed to elderly beneficiaries previously identified by Millennium bim’s local teams.

More than providing material assistance, the “Solidarity Soup” initiative sought to create meaningful moments of connection and sharing between the Bank’s employees and the beneficiary communities, promoting the values of solidarity, social inclusion and active citizenship.

According to Rui Pedro, Chairman of the Executive Committee of Millennium bim, “Volunteering is an integral part of Millennium bim’s culture and of the way our employees engage with the communities where they live and work. The ‘Solidarity Soup’ initiative is a clear example of their willingness to dedicate their time, energy and care to those who need it most, creating moments of sharing and human connection that go far beyond material support.”

The initiative relied on the voluntary participation of Millennium bim employees, who dedicated their time to this solidarity action, helping deliver support and meaningful moments of connection to hundreds of beneficiaries across the three provinces.
Through this initiative, Millennium bim combined corporate volunteering with direct social support, strengthening the relationship between its employees and the beneficiary communities.

Groww Q1 results: Net profit jumps 94.3% to ₹735 crore, revenue rises 66%
sum: The company's revenue from operations rose 66 per cent to ₹1,501.42 crore during the April-June quarter of FY27 from ₹904.40 crore a year earlier

Billionbrains Garage Ventures Ltd, the parent company of the digital investment platform Groww, on Wednesday reported a 94.3 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated Profit After Tax (PAT) to ₹735.04 crore for the quarter ended June 30.
Bengaluru-headquartered company had earned a PAT of ₹378.35 crore in the corresponding period last year.

On a sequential basis, revenue from operations remained largely flat at ₹1,501.42 crore, compared with ₹1,505.37 crore in the January-March quarter of FY26. PAT, however, increased from ₹686.36 crore in the preceding quarter.
Total expenses increased to ₹555.68 crore from ₹444.67 crore in the year-ago period.
Shares of the company were trading 3.7 per cent higher at ₹211.4 on the BSE in the afternoon trade.
(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

Bim Pepple transfer rumours with host of clubs linked with Plymouth Argyle striker
sum: A whole raft of clubs are reportedly interested in signing Pepple this summer
Plymouth Argyle striker Bim Pepple is wanted by a host of clubs, including Championship, MLS and a Champions League side, it has been reported.
FootballPark says that Bolton Wanderers and Sheffield United, Danish title holders AGF Aarhus, and a number of unnamed MLS sides are all said to be pursuing the 23-year-old.
Pepple arrived at Argyle from Luton Town, but after scoring 18 goals in all competitions during his first season with the Pilgrims, he is reportedly wanted by a host of clubs.

His form was so good over the second half of the 2025/26 campaign that it led to a first Canada international call-up in March, although he did not get the chance to make his debut in either of their games against Iceland or Tunisia.

Pepple was signed from Luton Town last summer, with reports suggesting Argyle paid an initial £250,000 for him but that could rise to around £600,000. But Pepple does have a release clause in his Argyle contract which has another three years to run.

FootballPark says that AGF Aarhus appear to be leading the chase by some distance. The reigning Danish Superligaen champions secured a place in next season's Champions League qualification rounds, and will take on Polish side Lech Poznan in the second qualifying round.
